glossary.LV: Left ventricle, the main pumping chamber that ejects blood into the aorta.
glossary.Angina: Chest pain from the heart muscle not getting enough oxygen.
glossary.Syncope: Brief loss of consciousness from reduced blood flow to the brain.
glossary.Presyncope: Feeling about to faint without actually losing consciousness.
glossary.Exertional dyspnoea: Breathlessness brought on by physical effort.
glossary.ICS: Intercostal space, the gap between two ribs.
glossary.Right upper sternal edge: The aortic area: 2nd intercostal space just right of the sternum.
glossary.Left sternal edge: The area just left of the breastbone where AR is best heard.
glossary.Carotids: The carotid arteries in the neck.
glossary.S1: First heart sound, from closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves.
glossary.Palpitations: An awareness of one's own heartbeat, often fast or irregular.
glossary.Rheumatic fever: Immune reaction weeks after strep throat that can scar heart valves.
glossary.Infective endocarditis: Infection of the heart's inner lining, usually the valves.
glossary.Cardiogenic shock: Circulatory failure because the heart cannot pump enough blood.
glossary.Acute heart failure: Sudden failure of the heart to pump adequately, causing fluid on the lungs.
glossary.Trans-valvular pressure gradient: Difference in pressure across a valve; higher means tighter stenosis.
glossary.mmHg: Millimetres of mercury, the unit for pressure.
glossary.Peak jet velocity: Fastest blood speed through the valve on echo; higher means more severe stenosis.
glossary.BNP: B-type natriuretic peptide, released by stretched ventricles; raised in heart failure.
glossary.Cardiomegaly: An enlarged heart on chest X-ray.
glossary.Pulmonary oedema: Fluid in the lungs, usually from a failing left heart.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs that make the kidneys pass more water and salt.
glossary.Fluid overload: Too much fluid in the body, causing swelling and breathlessness.
glossary.Carotid disease: Narrowing of the carotid arteries by atherosclerosis.
glossary.Cardiac output: Volume of blood the heart pumps each minute.
glossary.Decompensates: Stops coping, so the compensation fails and symptoms appear.
glossary.Mitral valve: Valve between the left atrium and left ventricle.
glossary.Mitral stenosis: Narrowing of the mitral valve, causing a mid-diastolic murmur.
glossary.Mid-diastolic murmur: A heart murmur heard in the middle of the filling phase.
glossary.Leaflet: One of the flaps of a heart valve.
glossary.Diastolic: During diastole, when the ventricles relax and fill.
glossary.Systolic: During systole, when the ventricles contract.
glossary.Regurgitant jet: The stream of blood flowing backwards through a leaky valve.
glossary.Cardiology: Branch of medicine dealing with the heart.
glossary.Red flag: A symptom or sign warning of serious disease needing urgent action.
glossary.Runoff: Rapid fall in aortic pressure as blood leaks back or drains away in diastole.
